correctness.rationale: Let m=a+1 and c=b+1. A primitive divisor s of p^(kc)-1 divides B=σ_k(p^b), has ord_s(p)=kc and s>c; divisibility forces s|m, hence m≥kc+1. A primitive divisor r of 2^(km)-1 (apart from the sole km=6 exception, immediately incompatible with m≥kc+1) divides A=σ_k(2^a), satisfies r>m>c, and therefore must equal p. Thus m|p-1; since s|m, p≡1 mod s, contradicting ord_s(p)=kc≥4. The finite verifier's 42,112 cases and zero hits corroborate but do not prove the infinite theorem.
